title: Gli sci di Primo Levi
overview: Thirty years after Primo Levi's death, Rai Cultura assembles a portrait that refuses to reduce him to the single label of Holocaust witness. Ten scholars, journalists and friends - among them the historian Carlo Ginzburg, the survivor and senator Liliana Segre, and his editor Ernesto Ferrero - each take up a different facet of a man who was novelist, poet, essayist, industrial chemist, amateur astronomer and mountaineer. Running through the film is the testimony of Ives Francisco, the young partisan arrested alongside Levi in the Aosta Valley in December 1943; the skis Levi left behind later carried Francisco into Switzerland and back again after the war, and give the film its title. Archive interviews return Levi's own voice on memory, work, writing and his Jewish roots.

overview: A dead-straight, endless road leading to nowhere ends at Nouadhibou, Mauritania, bordered by the ocean on one side and the Sahara on the other. A bleak departure point for tens of thousands pouring in from neighboring countries, all with one dream: Europe. Hotel Sahara is a film journey to the last invisible border separating West Africa and Europe. The bleak city on the Atlantic Coast is a metaphor, a point of arrival and departure, a gathering place of broken dreams—a no-man's land of endless waiting and hoping for a better life across the ocean. The film reveals how difficult it is to differentiate between "true" and "false" refugees. Is one "real" only when life and limb are threatened, or also when escaping a deadening lack of perspective? With an observant, cautious eye, Hotel Sahara documents how closely the dream of a better life is linked to sudden stagnancy, and the patience required to wait for years to finally, perhaps, arrive somewhere.

title: How is analytical R&D different from routine quality control?
original_title: How is analytical R&D different from routine quality control?
overview: Analytical R&D focuses on developing and improving analytical methods for new drugs, formulations, impurities, and stability studies. It helps determine the best way to test a pharmaceutical product during development.  Routine Quality Control (QC), on the other hand, uses approved and validated methods to test finished products and raw materials against set quality standards before release.  In simple terms, analytical R&D develops and validates the testing methods, while routine QC uses those methods to check product quality consistently. Both are important for maintaining safe, effective, and reliable pharmaceutical products.

title: Can Molkem investigate pharmaceutical impurities?
overview: Yes, Molkem can support the investigation of pharmaceutical impurities through its analytical R&D services. Impurity investigation is an important part of pharmaceutical development because unwanted impurities can affect the quality, stability, safety, and performance of a drug substance or finished product.  As part of analytical research and development in pharmaceutical industry, impurity studies can support method development, method validation, stability testing, specification setting, quality investigations, and regulatory submissions. These studies help pharmaceutical companies understand impurity profiles and monitor changes during manufacturing and storage.  https://www.molkem.com/analytical-research-and-development-in-pharmaceutical-industry

title: When is analytical method validation required?
original_title: When is analytical method validation required?
overview: Analytical method validation is required when a new analytical method is developed or when an existing method is changed significantly. In the pharmaceutical industry, validation confirms that a method is suitable for its intended purpose and can provide accurate, reliable, and consistent results. It is commonly required for assay testing, impurity testing, stability studies, release testing, and regulatory submissions.  As part of analytical research and development in pharmaceutical industry, method validation may also be required when an analytical method is transferred to another laboratory, when there are major changes in the product or manufacturing process, or when the testing procedure is modified.  A reliable analytical R&D pharma process helps ensure that analytical methods meet their intended requirements and generate dependable results.

Molkem also provides testing for impurities such as nitrosamines, genotoxic, elemental, process-related, and degradation impurities, where applicable.

Each person holds a unique view of the landscape, the neighborhood, and the construction sites, weaving their own narrative around them.  The film explores how this environmental shift resonates with them—deep within their inner selves and sensibilities—and what they expect from it. It follows those who daily traverse these varied paths: riverbanks, crumbling sandpits, stairways, footbridges, public squares, broad avenues, and bike lanes, alongside elements of street furniture that are aging, ephemeral, or newly built. Revealing and discussing improvisation's benefits onstage and off, via the 'yes and' mentality and 'improv equals life' philosophy, 'Off the Cuff' demonstrates that there is more depth to improvisation than simply silly comedy.

overview: In Germany, the forest is more than the sum of its trees: it is a myth, the backdrop to a grand German drama. German culture, it is said, has its roots in the forest, at least since Germanic warriors defeated the Romans in the Battle of Varus. During the Romantic era, the forest became a place of longing; it was painted, written about in poetry, and celebrated in song—and at the same time, it once again became a symbol of national sovereignty. title: What are the five main steps of developing a drug?

overview: The new drug development process is a long and carefully planned journey that takes a potential medicine from early research to approval and continued safety monitoring. The main phases of pharmaceutical development include discovery and development, preclinical research, clinical development, regulatory review, and post-market monitoring. During the discovery stage, researchers identify and study promising drug candidates to understand how they may work and select suitable candidates for further development. In preclinical research, the candidate is evaluated through laboratory and nonclinical studies to understand its safety, pharmacology, toxicity, and other important properties before it is tested in humans. The next stage is the clinical development of drug candidates, where clinical trials are conducted in different phases to evaluate safety, dosage, effectiveness, and possible side effects.

title: Does PLC affect property resale value?
original_title: Does PLC affect property resale value?
overview: Yes, PLC can affect the resale value of a property, but it does not always increase the resale price by the same amount as the original PLC charges paid to the builder. PLC, or Preferential Location Charges, are usually paid for a more desirable position within a project, such as a park-facing, corner, higher-floor, or better-view property.  A property with a preferred location may attract more buyers during resale because of better views, natural light, ventilation, privacy, or other location benefits. However, the resale value mainly depends on factors such as the property's overall condition, location, project demand, market prices, and buyer preference.  Therefore, while PLC in real estate can add value to a property, buyers should not assume that every rupee paid as PLC charges in real estate will be recovered separately at the time of resale. The actual benefit depends on the demand for that particular property and its location.

title: What is the average PLC rate in Ahmedabad?
original_title: What is the average PLC rate in Ahmedabad?
overview: The average PLC rate in Ahmedabad can vary from one project to another, as there is no fixed PLC rate in real estate. In many residential projects, the PLC rate may range from around ₹100 to ₹300 per sq. ft. The actual rate depends on the property's location, floor, view, and other preferred features.  For example, a park-facing, garden-facing, corner, pool-facing, road-facing, or higher-floor apartment may have additional PLC charges in real estate because these locations are considered more desirable.  The total PLC charges depend on both the PLC rate and the property area. For instance, if the PLC rate is ₹200 per sq. ft. and the applicable area is 1,200 sq. ft., the PLC charges would be ₹2,40,000.  Therefore, buyers should always confirm the PLC meaning in real estate, applicable PLC rate, and total PLC charges with the builder before booking a property in Ahmedabad.

title: What is a typical PLC rate in India?

The total PLC can be calculated as:  PLC Charges = PLC Rate × Property Area  For example, if the PLC rate is ₹200 per sq. ft. for a 1,000 sq. ft. property, the PLC charges would be ₹2,00,000. overview: Drug discovery and drug development are two connected but different stages in bringing a new medicine to patients. Drug discovery is the early part of the drug discovery and development process, where scientists search for potential medicines by studying diseases, biological targets, chemical compounds, and their effects. Researchers identify promising molecules, screen them, and carry out laboratory studies to understand how they may work against a particular disease. The main goal of drug discovery is to find a suitable drug candidate that has the potential to provide a useful therapeutic effect.  Drug development starts after a promising candidate has been identified. It involves a much broader and more detailed process to determine whether the candidate can be developed into a safe, effective, and reliable medicine.  https://www.molkem.com/blog/pharmaceutical-drug-development-process#definition
